faq: Do you change my prices automatically?

Only with your approval. We prepare the change list, you accept or edit it, and then we update prices in bulk. Automated repricing rules are set up in Premium, using Amazon's own tool and a floor you choose.
Do you need my cost data?
Yes, a cost per unit for each product, including freight and prep. Without that, we can only show fees and revenue. A simple sheet or even an email list is enough.
Where do competitor prices come from?
We look at the public Buy Box and offer pages on Amazon, by hand. We do not use scraped data or tools that break Amazon's terms, and we never copy or fix prices with other sellers.
Can you help if I am losing the Buy Box?
We look at price, shipping speed and stock as possible causes, and tell you which one seems to matter. The Buy Box is Amazon's decision, so we explain the factors and cannot promise to win it.

desc:
An Amazon pricing review with fees and margins shows what you really keep from each sale. Ecom Swift LLC lists your referral, FBA and storage fees against your product costs, compares public prices for the same items and suggests price changes for you to approve.

## What is an Amazon pricing review?

A pricing review is a structured check of what each product costs you, what Amazon takes, and what is left. It starts with your selling price and subtracts the product cost, the referral fee, fulfilment and storage charges, and any other costs you add. The result is the true margin per item, which is often different from what the price suggests.

It also looks outward. Public offers for the same product show where your price sits in the market, so you can see which items are too high, too low or about right.

## Why old prices stop working

Amazon fees are not fixed. Referral and fulfilment charges change, storage costs rise at busy times, and your own supplier prices move. A price set a year ago may no longer cover what it did then. Some sellers only discover this when a bank statement looks thinner than expected.

Prices that are too low give away profit on every order. Prices that are too high can push a product out of the Buy Box or away from shoppers who compare similar listings. Neither shows clearly in daily sales figures, so an item can look busy while quietly losing money.

## How pricing choices affect profit and sales

Price influences both the number of orders and the money left from each. Knowing your true margin lets you decide with facts: raise prices where there is room, hold them where demand is thin, and drop products that cannot cover their costs at any fair price.

Competing offers matter because Amazon shoppers compare. A price that is out of line with similar offers can reduce clicks and orders. Results still depend on reviews, images, stock and shipping speed, and we make no claim about sales or Buy Box wins. We also avoid any tactic that breaks Amazon's fair pricing policy.

## What a thorough pricing review includes

- Product costs entered for each item, including shipping to your warehouse.
- Referral and FBA fees counted against the current price.
- Storage and other recurring charges considered.
- True margin worked out per product.
- A flag for items that lose money or have room to rise.
- Competing public offers reviewed by hand.
- Minimum price rules suggested for each product.
- A bulk price update file ready to upload.
- A reusable margin and fee sheet, with a review calendar in the top package.

## How we carry it out

We ask for your cost data and match it to your product list in Seller Central. We pull your fee details from Amazon's own fee information for each item and put every figure into one sheet. For items in scope, we look at public offers on the same product page and note where your price sits.

We then prepare a list of changes with reasons. You approve each change, and we can load them in bulk through an update file. In the larger packages we also set repricing rules inside Seller Central with minimum prices, so automated changes cannot drop below a safe floor. We do not change prices without your approval.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep your cost data accurate, including packaging and inbound freight.
- Set a minimum price for every product before using any repricing rule.
- Check your margin again when Amazon announces fee changes.
- Compare only identical products, not look-alikes.
- Review prices on a calendar, not only after problems.

**Avoid:**
- Matching a competitor's price without checking your own margin.
- Running repricing rules with no minimum.
- Agreeing prices with other sellers.
- Ignoring storage and return costs in your math.
- Raising every price by the same amount.

## Who this is for

This service suits a seller who suspects some products lose money after fees. It also suits an owner who has not looked at prices since the first listing and wants a sanity check. A wholesale seller with many items can use the bulk update file and fee sheet to keep a long catalog consistent.

## What we need from you

Please send your product costs, either in a sheet or an invoice list, along with your minimum profit target. You invite us as a user in your Seller Central account with permission to view products and fees. We never ask for your password, and we do not change a price until you approve it.
